# EAS build failed because the lockfile was generated by a newer npm than EAS runs

**Date**: 2026-08-17
**Type**: bug
**Summary**: npm 11 lockfiles omit hoisted peer deps that EAS's npm 10 `npm ci` demands
**Context**: .minerva/work/2026-08-17-toddler-coloring-app (see git history if the worktree has been cleaned up)

## Context

The first `eas build --platform ios --profile production` failed 16 seconds in, during
`INSTALL_DEPENDENCIES`, long before anything to do with signing or Xcode. EAS reported only
"Unknown error. See logs of the Install dependencies build phase", which points at the wrong
thing — the failure is entirely local to dependency resolution.

Reading the actual log is worth knowing how to do: `eas build:list --json` gives a
`logFiles[0]` URL, and that file is **brotli-encoded** (`x-goog-stored-content-encoding: br`).
`curl --compressed` does not decode it; `file` reports "data". Decompress it with Python's
`brotli` module. Each line is then JSON with the real output in `msg`.

## Finding

The build runs `npm ci --include=dev`, which failed with:

```
npm ci can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json are in sync.
Missing: @emnapi/core@1.11.3 from lock file
Missing: @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3 from lock file
```

Root cause is an npm version mismatch, not a bad dependency. `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime`
declares `@emnapi/core` and `@emnapi/runtime` as **peer** dependencies. npm 11 (local,
Node 24) resolves them only nested under `node_modules/@unrs/resolver-binding-wasm32-wasi/`
and writes a lockfile with no top-level entries for them. npm 10 — which is what EAS's
Node 22.23.1 image ships — expects those peers hoisted, finds them absent, and refuses the
lockfile. `npm ci` passes locally and fails on EAS from the *same* committed lockfile.

The chain reaches the project through `eslint-config-expo` → `unrs-resolver`, so it is
entirely a devDependency concern — and EAS installs devDependencies, so it still breaks the
native build.

Fixed by regenerating the lockfile with the npm EAS actually uses,
`npx npm@10 install --package-lock-only`, which hoists both packages. Verified afterwards
that `npm ci --include=dev` succeeds under **both** npm 10 and npm 11 — npm 11 accepts an
npm-10-generated lockfile, so the compatibility only fails in one direction.

## Implications

**Node 24 is not available on EAS.** The SDK 57 image is pinned to Node 22.23.1, so the
mismatch cannot be fixed by raising the build environment to match a modern local toolchain —
the lockfile has to be kept compatible with npm 10. `eas.json` now pins `node: "22.23.1"` and
`ios.image: "sdk-57"` on every profile so the build environment is explicit rather than
whatever `auto` resolves to next.

Anyone adding or upgrading a dependency on a machine running npm 11 will silently reintroduce
this: local `npm ci` still passes, so nothing catches it until a build burns a queue slot.
After touching dependencies, regenerate with `npx npm@10 install --package-lock-only` and
confirm with `npx npm@10 ci --include=dev --dry-run` before pushing.

Note that `image` is **platform-scoped** in `eas.json` — `build.production.image` is rejected
by the CLI as "not allowed"; it belongs under `build.production.ios.image`. `eas config
--platform ios --profile production` validates the file and prints the resolved profile,
which is much faster than discovering a schema error by starting a build.
